samples.summary: New paste-refusal exemption (a cut's own blocks) is not recorded in the canonical design doc
samples.evidence: The delta adds a second exemption to the `merge-paste-partial` rule: `planPasteMerges` now filters the cut's own travelling blocks out of the destination split check (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2428-2437). The canonical subsystem doc's copy/paste bullet still states only the one exemption — "A paste that would only partially overwrite a block is refused whole (`merge-paste-partial`, ...); a single-cell destination is exempt, since it writes through the merge anchor" (docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:103-107). The decision is captured only in the working task file docs/tasks/active/20260912-sheets-paste-merge-propagation-todo.md:56-61, which is a transient task note, not the design record. CONTRIBUTING's design-doc discipline expects the behaviour rule to be folded into the subsystem doc, and the PR already updated that same bullet in an earlier commit — so this is a divergence the delta introduced, not a pre-existing gap.

samples.summary: Anchor-exclusion set duplicates `moveRangeTo`'s `movedAnchors` pattern instead of a shared helper
samples.evidence: `planPasteMerges` builds `travelling = new Set(...map(toSref))` and filters `getMergesIntersecting(destRange)` by it (sheet.ts:2432-2437), which is line-for-line the shape `moveRangeTo` already uses at sheet.ts:2612-2616 (`movedAnchors` + same filter + same `isRangeInRange` partial check). The task doc for this work explicitly asked to reuse/extract rather than write a second implementation of merge helpers (docs/tasks/active/20260912-sheets-paste-merge-propagation-todo.md:27-29). The duplication is three lines and behaviourally identical today, so the cost is only that the two split-refusal rules can drift apart; no user-visible impact.
